# Asolaria 81-body quantum and gravity CPU test — evaluation

**Evidence:** nine SHA-seeded local hidden-variable Bell waves, a programmed singlet reference, nine 81-site GHZ sampler waves, nine spatial scaling checks, independent Python 3.11 / 3.13 runs. Both CI result JSON files are byte-identical SHA-256 `f3c634d62c8ebb634aa6fbd04503f94c2bee3cc1269880a6b69b4db896234dd0`.

**Quantum:** Each local deterministic 4,096-sample CHSH wave has S=2, consistent with Bell locality. The explicit singlet Born-rule model has S=2√2≈2.828427, but this is programmed mathematics. The GHZ sampler passed restricted all-X, all-Z, and mixed-basis tests, but these bases and tests are classically reproducible. Neither quantum entanglement nor FTL signaling was measured.

**Gravity:** Position-independent metadata hashes remain stable by construction. With no position-dependent potential, the metadata-only force is zero. An explicitly inserted U∝−1/r potential produces F∝1/r² and a 10× distance ratio of 1/100; an explicitly inserted U∝−1/r² light-gradient potential produces F∝1/r³ and 1/1000. Pair anti-symmetry, translation and rotation covariance passed. Neither force is emergent in this code; both were specified in advance.

**Conclusion:** simulation reference controls pass, but the Asolaria metadata alone was not shown to produce gravitational dynamics, quantum entanglement, or distance-free physical communication. Independent optical / GPU experiments require actual data, calibrated clocks and controls.

See https://github.com/JesseBrown1980/asolaria-stone-to-moss/actions/runs/38589387275 and the original test code.
